concepts.name: Test-first principle
concepts.summary: Understand that the test is written before the production code it exercises and why that ordering matters.

concepts.name: Failing test as specification
concepts.summary: Describe how a failing test states one small piece of required behaviour before it exists.

concepts.name: Red-green-refactor cycle
concepts.summary: Explain the three steps of writing a failing test, making it pass, then cleaning up, and why they occur in that order.

concepts.name: Smallest step to pass
concepts.summary: Recognise that in the green step you write only enough code to make the current failing test pass.

concepts.name: Fast feedback from test runs
concepts.summary: Understand why running the tests after each small change quickly shows whether the last change broke something.

concepts.name: Refactoring under green tests
concepts.summary: Remember that refactoring changes structure without changing behaviour and is done only while all tests pass.

misconceptions.text: TDD means writing all the tests for a feature up front and then writing all the code.
A test that fails at the start means something has gone wrong.
Refactoring means adding new features to make the code better.

concepts.name: Writing a single failing unit test
concepts.summary: Write one focused unit test that fails for the right reason, using arrange-act-assert structure.

concepts.name: Fake it and obvious implementation
aliases: fake it till you make it
concepts.summary: Pass a test with a hard-coded value or direct implementation and choose between them based on confidence.

concepts.name: Triangulation by added examples
concepts.summary: Add a second test case with different data to force a hard-coded result to become a general implementation.

concepts.name: Choosing the next test
concepts.summary: Keep a list of behaviours to test and pick the next simple case that moves the design forward.

concepts.name: Removing duplication in refactoring
concepts.summary: Spot duplication in code and tests during the refactor step and remove it while keeping the tests green.

concepts.name: Test naming and readability
concepts.summary: Name tests after the behaviour they check so a failure message explains what broke.

concepts.name: Verifying the test fails first
concepts.summary: Run a new test before implementing to confirm it fails for the expected reason and does not pass vacuously.

misconceptions.text: Hard-coding a return value to pass a test is cheating and should be avoided.
If a new test passes immediately, that is a good sign and no check is needed.
Refactoring only applies to production code, not to the tests.

concepts.name: Tests driving design
concepts.summary: Analyse how difficulty in writing a test reveals coupling or poor responsibilities and change the design in response.

concepts.name: Dependency injection for testability
concepts.summary: Introduce seams so collaborators can be supplied from outside and replaced in tests.

concepts.name: Test doubles for isolation
concepts.summary: Use stubs, fakes and mocks to isolate the unit under test from slow or nondeterministic collaborators.

concepts.name: Behaviour versus implementation testing
concepts.summary: Distinguish tests that assert observable behaviour from those coupled to internals and rewrite the latter.

concepts.name: Testing legacy code safely
concepts.summary: Analyse untested code and add characterization tests before changing it.

concepts.name: Edge cases and error paths
concepts.summary: Drive boundary values, invalid input and failure handling through tests added one at a time.

concepts.name: Test suite speed and independence
concepts.summary: Diagnose tests that depend on shared state, order or slow resources and restructure them to be fast and independent.

misconceptions.text: Every collaborator should be mocked so each class is tested in complete isolation.
High code coverage from TDD proves the tests are good.
TDD can only be used on new code, not on existing code.

concepts.name: Outside-in and inside-out TDD
concepts.summary: Evaluate the classicist and mockist styles and choose between them for a given design context.

concepts.name: Acceptance-test-driven outer loop
concepts.summary: Analyse how a failing acceptance test drives inner unit-level TDD cycles toward a feature.

concepts.name: Test suite maintainability audit
concepts.summary: Evaluate a suite for smells such as fragility, obscure tests and duplication, and judge which to fix first.

concepts.name: Test pyramid balance
concepts.summary: Judge the mix of unit, integration and end-to-end tests so TDD remains fast and confidence is adequate.

concepts.name: Evolutionary design with TDD
concepts.summary: Analyse how small refactorings under tests let architecture emerge and when upfront design is still needed.

concepts.name: TDD in hard domains
concepts.summary: Evaluate strategies for applying TDD to user interfaces, databases, concurrency and external services.

concepts.name: Mutation testing as feedback
concepts.summary: Use mutation analysis to find tests that run code without truly verifying it.

misconceptions.text: There is one correct style of TDD and the other style is a mistake.
TDD replaces the need for acceptance and integration testing.
Following TDD guarantees a good architecture without any deliberate design thinking.

concepts.name: Adapting TDD to context
concepts.summary: Judge when strict TDD, relaxed test-after or spikes are most economical given risk, uncertainty and codebase.

concepts.name: Spike and discard practice
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to explore with throwaway code and then reimplement it test-first.

concepts.name: Evidence on TDD outcomes
concepts.summary: Critically appraise empirical studies of TDD's effect on quality, productivity and design and their limitations.

concepts.name: Designing team TDD adoption
concepts.summary: Create a plan for introducing TDD to a team, including katas, pairing, mob sessions and shared conventions.

concepts.name: Test architecture for large systems
concepts.summary: Design a test architecture with contract tests, test data strategies and build pipeline stages that keeps TDD feedback fast at scale.

concepts.name: Property-based test-driven design
concepts.summary: Combine example-driven cycles with property-based tests to specify general behaviour and discover edge cases.

concepts.name: Evolving legacy systems with TDD
concepts.summary: Create incremental strategies that bring large untested systems under test while delivering change.

misconceptions.text: Experts apply strict test-first to every line of code without exception.
Studies have conclusively proven that TDD always improves quality and productivity.
Mandating TDD with a coverage target is enough to get a team to adopt it well.
